title: Sample count bound per coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. If $M$ is the sample count per coefficient chosen for accuracy $\varepsilon$ and total confidence $\delta$, then, viewed as a rational number, $M\le 16|\mathcal F|^2L/\varepsilon^2$, where $L$ is the failure-bit count associated with confidence parameter $\delta/|\mathcal F|$.
